gaps: Local sales and use taxes (county, city, RTD and other districts) are listed only for Denver and Colorado Springs, read on the official county pages; the state DR 1002 table could not be read for this release, so elsewhere type your combined local rate.
Some counties and regional transportation authorities add their own registration fees, and the DMV list mentions a county road and bridge fee without an amount; the line is shown without an amount.
The specific ownership tax is computed on 85% of the MSRP; without an MSRP the engine uses the price, which misstates the tax on a used car. The year of service is counted from the model year.

The statute (C.R.S. 42-3-306(2)(b)(V)) also provides a second, adjustable age-based fee; the DMV publishes a single age-of-vehicle fee table ($12, $10, $7) effective July 1, 2026, which the engine uses.
The $0.50 insurance fee the DMV lists is not added: the page does not make clear which vehicles pay it.

The electric vehicle fee ($63.05 for 2026-27) is indexed each fiscal year; renewals after June 2027 use the same amount until DMV publishes the next one. Renewal-year road safety and EV road usage amounts assume a fall renewal.
No dealer handling fee cap was read on an official page, and whether that fee is taxed was not found; it is left out of the taxed price.

singular: Colorado’s yearly specific ownership tax is figured on 85% of the original MSRP: 2.1% in the first year of service, 1.5% in the second, 1.2% in the third, 0.9% in the fourth, then 0.45% until the tenth year, when it drops to a flat $3 [crs-42-3-107].
The state sales tax on a car is only 2.9%, but local taxes stack on top: a Denver resident pays 9.15% in all, including the RTD tax and Denver’s 5.15% [denver-tax].
In Colorado Springs the county, the Pikes Peak Rural Transportation Authority and the city add 1.23%, 1% and 3.07% to the state rate [elpaso-tax].
The registration base fee for a car rises by 20 cents per 100 lb from $6 at 2,000 lb, and by 60 cents per 100 lb above 4,500 lb [crs-42-3-306].
Two FASTER surcharges fund roads and bridges: $19.30 and $18 a year for a car of 2,001 to 5,000 lb, the road part rising to $23 on September 1, 2027 [dmv-fees].
Electric and plug-in hybrid owners pay a $63.05 electric vehicle fee plus a road usage fee of $26 or $13 for registrations from July 2026, scheduled to reach $96 and $27 by 2031-32 [dmv-ev].
Both battery electric cars and plug-in hybrids pay the equalization fee, which can be paid in installments [dmv-ev-page].

In the Front Range program area, gasoline and hybrid cars more than seven model years old need a $35 emissions test every two years, and the seller must provide one when the car changes owner [dmv-emissions].
The emissions area covers all or parts of nine counties from Douglas to Larimer and Weld [cdphe-area].
Plates cost $7.38 in material fees and a transfer of ownership title $7.20 [dmv-title].
